details: CONFIRMED by reading the item, the diff and the fixer report. The item promises two things: records do not land naming missing commits,
and the PR merge is gated "or the docs say plainly it is not". The second has a documented alternative and is met by docs/setup.md:71-73.
The first has no documentation-only alternative in the pass case ("docs and setup state it and relay keeps the records out"). Meeting it
needs a decision on where check records live for squash projects (tree files under .relay/checks vs a git notes ref / a side ref / a
per-machine store, or a guard exception letting an agent git-rm a branch's records before its PR), which changes the design of
docs/plans/review-gate.md section 4.1 (relay_marks: "the only code that reads or writes .relay/checks on a task branch").
Owner context in the brief (29 Oct): relay never squashes and squash projects are outside relay land; that leans toward answer (a) of the
owner question, but it is the owner's to give.
Design: whether a squash-merge project keeps relay's check records as tree files on its default branch (documented limit) or relay moves
them out of the squashed tree.
Size: 5 for (a) (amend the item's pass case); 60+ for (b).
evidence: relay queue show squash-merge-projects-keep-check-records-of-lost -> Pass cases: "After the same squash-merge, no record on main names a
commit main lacks (or the docs and setup state it and relay keeps the records out of the squashed tree)."
fixer report: "Documented the limit in docs/setup.md ... Not decided: keeping records out of the squash (needs owner)."
git diff --stat master...HEAD -> docs/setup.md +5, tests/test_setup.py +8, gate log; no code change.
failing_case: Queue item pass case: "After the same squash-merge, no record on main names a commit main lacks (or the docs and setup state it AND
relay keeps the records out of the squashed tree)". On the head: a temp repo with .relay/ on main, branch wt/x with a check record
.relay/checks/<sha-of-wt/x-head>.json, squash-merged into main, wt/x deleted -> main holds that file and `git cat-file -e <sha>` fails
on main. Neither branch of the pass case holds: the record is on main, and relay does nothing to keep it out (the change only documents it).
The fixer's own report says so ("Not decided: keeping records out of the squash (needs owner)"), yet the branch is reported DONE and the
cycle would close the item with `relay queue done`, so the open half disappears from the queue.
fix_hint: Ask the owner: (a) accept the documented limit and amend the item's pass case, or (b) a design item for keeping records out of a
squashed tree. Do not close the item with the current pass case.
pass_cases: 1. Owner answers "document only" -> the queue item's pass case is amended (relay queue edit) to "docs and setup state the limit", the
docs/setup.md lines 71-75 stay, and the item closes; this is an owner entry on F1.
2. Owner answers "keep records out" -> after a squash-merge of a branch with a check record in a temp repo, main has no file under
.relay/checks naming a commit main does not contain (git cat-file -e fails for none).
3. Either way, on a fast-forward merge (relay land, merge --ff-only wt/<name>) the records of the merged head stay readable on main
(relay_marks reads <head>.json at the default branch) and the merge gate still refuses a head with no gate/review/check.
reason: Owner said document only; docs/setup.md:71-75 states the limit.
findings.summary: the item's pass case is not met: records still land on main naming commits it lacks, and relay does not keep them out of the squash

failing_case: Setting a new project up (or the --relay-folder form) writes .relay/README.md from RELAY_README, which says
"A merge into the default branch is refused until the branch's last commit has its gate, its review and its check." with no word that a
pull request squash-merged on the server is not gated and carries the checks/ files. An agent or person in arsenal reads that README,
not relay's docs/setup.md. The pass case says "the docs and setup state it"; setup states nothing new.
Should: the README text names the limit in one or two lines (merges made through relay only; a server-side squash is not gated and keeps
the checks/ files, naming commits of the deleted branch).
fix_hint: Add to RELAY_README under checks/: "Only merges made through relay (relay land, the merge hook) are refused; a pull request
squash-merged on the server is not gated, and its checks/ files then name commits of the deleted branch." Copy the same text into
relay's own .relay/README.md; add the test of pass case 1.

2. relay's own .relay/README.md equals relay_setup.RELAY_README (tests/test_queue.py:513 keeps passing: update both together).

details: CONFIRMED by reading merge.py's docstring. Narrower than the truth rather than wrong in the case that matters (squash), so LOW.
Size: 5.
evidence: plugins/relay/hooks/merge.py:5-7 "PreToolUse = the merge gate (section 7: refuses the merge, exit 2, one line), PostToolUse = the
failing_case: docs/setup.md:71 "Limit: this holds for merges made by `relay land`, which never squashes." A reader concludes that an agent's
`git merge --ff-only wt/x` in a Claude Code session is not gated; it is (plugins/relay/hooks/merge.py, PreToolUse, "the merge gate
(section 7: refuses the merge)"). What is not gated is a merge made outside relay's hooks: a server-side pull-request merge, or a
person's own git in a terminal.
fix_hint: "Limit: this holds for merges relay makes or sees (relay land and an agent's `git merge --ff-only wt/<name>`), which never squash."
pass_cases: 1. The limit sentence names both gated paths: relay land and an agent's `git merge --ff-only wt/<name>` (the merge hook).
2. It still says a server-side squash merge is not gated and carries the checks/ files naming commits of the deleted branch.
reason: docs/setup.md:71 names the merge hook and git merge --ff-only wt/<name>; asserted in the doc test.
findings.summary: the limit says the gate holds only for merges made by `relay land`; the merge hook also gates an agent's `git merge --ff-only wt/<name>`
